basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum. Necessario sancta Scriptura multoties reperit quod vidit'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum. Necessario sancta Scriptura multoties reperit quod vidit Deus bona esse quae fecit, ut hinc informaretur pietas fidelium; non tamen pro humano sensu, qui saepe etiam bonis rebus offenditur, quarum causas atque ordinem nescit, de creatura visibili atque invisibili judicare, sed laudanti Deo credere et cedere. Tanto enim quisque facilius aliquid proficiendo cognoscit, quanto religiosius antequam cognosceret Deo credidit. Vidit ergo Deus quod essent bona quae fecit, quoniam quae facienda placebant, ut fierent, facta placuerunt, ut manerent, quantum cuique rei existendi sive manendi a tanto fabricatore fuerat constituenda mensura.
